caption: A dropper elevator: the hopper under the input chest feeds the bottom of a column of six droppers facing up; the top one pushes into the output chest five blocks above the input chest. One observer clock fires the whole column: the observer whose back touches the second dropper pulses every 6 gt with its partner (placed last: a player starts the clock by placing it), and a chain of four observers carries each pulse up to the observer powering the fifth dropper, 4 gt later in the period. A powered dropper powers the droppers above and below it, so each powered dropper fires three. The 4 gt keep the upper group off whenever the lower group's top dropper is updated: that dropper also reads the upper group's power (quasi-connectivity: a dropper is powered when the block above it would be) and would otherwise stay triggered and never fire again.

A dropper elevator ten blocks up: the hopper under the input chest feeds a column of eleven droppers facing up, the top one pushing into the output chest. One observer clock (6 gt, its partner placed last as a player starts it) fires the column through a chain of observers facing down: the observer whose back touches a dropper powers it hard, and a hard-powered dropper powers the ones above and below it. The clock's own observer fires droppers 0-2; a four-observer bend carries the pulse to the observer firing droppers 3-5 4 gt later; then a straight chain climbs a block every 2 gt and an observer every two blocks fires the next three droppers 4 gt after the ones below. A dropper also reads the power of the dropper two above (quasi-connectivity), so each group must be off whenever the group below turns off: the 4 gt offsets keep it so.

Same family as lift5-chain-14b and lift10-chain-28b: each two more blocks of height add two droppers, two chain observers and one.

A dropper elevator 4 blocks up (13 blocks): the hopper under the input chest feeds a column of droppers facing up, the top one pushing into the output chest. One observer clock (6 gt, its partner placed last: a player starts it) fires the column through a chain of observers facing down; the observer whose back touches a dropper powers it hard, and a hard-powered dropper powers the ones above and below it. The clock's own observer fires droppers 0-2, a four-observer bend fires 3-5 4 gt later, then every two blocks of a straight chain fire the next three 4 gt after the ones below: a dropper also reads the power of the dropper two above (quasi-connectivity), so each group must be off whenever the group below turns off.
